subject: chemistry
title: Atom economy
key_idea: (Separate chemistry) The atom economy of a reaction is the percentage of the mass of the reactants that ends up as the desired product. A high atom economy means less waste. A reaction pathway is chosen using atom economy, yield, rate, cost and by-products.

blocks.text: (Separate chemistry) Atom economy shows how much of the starting materials end up as useful products. This section covers what it means and why it matters.

items.meaning: A measure of the amount of starting materials that end up as useful products. It is calculated from the balanced equation.
The product you want to make.
A product that is not wanted, such as water in a neutralisation.

items: A high atom economy means most of the reactant mass becomes the desired product.
It is important for sustainable development, because less raw material is wasted.
It is also important for economic reasons, because wasted atoms are wasted money.
Atom economy shows how much of the reactants becomes the desired product.
A high atom economy means less waste.
It matters for sustainability and for cost.

blocks.text: Use the balanced equation and the Mr values. Multiply each Mr by its balancing number.

blocks.label: Percentage atom economy
blocks.formula: atom economy = (Mr of the desired product ÷ sum of the Mr of all the reactants) × 100
where: Use the balancing numbers from the equation.
The sum of the Mr of the reactants equals the sum of the Mr of the products.

items.text: 2PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂. The desired product is lead.

items: The answer must be less than 100%.
If the desired product is the only product, the atom economy is 100%.
Use the total of all products instead of all reactants if you prefer. Both totals are the same.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating percentage atom economy from relative formula masses.
working: Atom economy = Mr of desired product ÷ sum of Mr of all reactants × 100
diagram.question: A reaction makes a desired product with a relative formula mass of **{d}**. The relative formula masses of all the reactants add up to **{t}**. Calculate the percentage atom economy.

items: Atom economy = Mr of desired product ÷ total Mr of reactants × 100.
The answer is less than 100% when there is a waste product.

blocks.text: (Higher tier for AQA) Atom economy is not the only factor. Industry chooses a pathway using several types of data.

rows: A high value means less waste.
A high yield means more product from the same reactants.
A fast reaction makes product sooner.
For a reversible reaction, it decides how much product forms.
A useful by-product can be sold, which reduces waste.
Raw materials, catalyst, high temperature and high pressure all cost money.

blocks.text: Example: hydrogen from methane and steam, CH₄ + H₂O → CO + 3H₂, has an atom economy of 17.6%. Hydrogen from ammonia, 2NH₃ → N₂ + 3H₂, has the same value, so the choice depends on the other factors.

items: Compare atom economy, yield, rate, equilibrium, by-products and cost.
A reaction with a lower atom economy can still be chosen.
Use the data given in the question to justify the choice.

checks.q: State what is meant by atom economy.
checks.a: A measure of the amount of starting materials that end up as useful products.

checks.q: KOH + HCl → KCl + H₂O. Calculate the atom economy for making KCl. (Mr: KOH = 56.0, HCl = 36.5, KCl = 74.5, H₂O = 18.0)
Give two factors, other than atom economy, to consider when choosing a reaction pathway.
checks.a: Any two from: percentage yield, rate of reaction, equilibrium position, usefulness of by-products, cost of raw materials, energy requirement.

worked_example.question:
The equation for the reaction is:

AgNO₃(aq) + NaI(aq) → AgI(s) + NaNO₃(aq)

Relative formula masses (Mr): AgNO₃ = 170, NaI = 150, AgI = 235, NaNO₃ = 85

Calculate the percentage atom economy for the production of silver iodide in this reaction.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: The total of the products, 235 + 85 = 320, also scores the first mark.

worked_example.question:
Lead can be obtained by heating its oxide with carbon.

The balanced equation for the reaction is

2PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂

Calculate the atom economy for the production of lead in this reaction.

(relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16, Pb = 207; relative formula masses: PbO = 223, CO₂ = 44)

Give your answer to two significant figures.
worked_example.tip: The correct answer, 90, scores all four marks even without working.

worked_example.question:
This is the equation for the reaction in the experiment.

NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

Water is a waste product in this reaction.

Calculate the atom economy for the reaction.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): H = 1.0, O = 16.0, Na = 23.0, Cl = 35.5
answer_points: Mr of NaCl = 58.5 and Mr of H₂O = 18.0, so the total Mr = 76.5 (1)
